## The Gradual Irrationality Reduction Program

You can't just stop being stupid immediately; it's like weaning a baby off eating paint chips. You can't just take away all the paint chips at once. They'll cry. You have to gradually replace paint chips with food until they forget paint chips were ever an option. So this book teaches you to be less stupid gradually:
- Year 1: Move 1% of murder money to medicine money (baby steps)
- Year 2: "Hey, we didn't die! Let's do 2%!"
- Year 5: "Remember when we spent money on bombs? That was weird."
- Year 10: "What's a war?"
- Year 20: "We used to WHAT?!"

After 80 years of observation, I've decoded the correct paper-giving sequence:

**Step 1: Get Many Papers.** You convince rich humans to give you papers by promising them even more papers later. This is called "investment," which is gambling but wearing a suit. There are approximately 2,800 humans with a billion papers. Statistically, at least one of them prefers living.

**Step 2: Give Papers to Loud Humans.** If you give loud humans papers, they become loud about your thing instead of other things. This is called "marketing," which is lying but with graphics.

**Step 3: Give Papers to the Humans Who Give Papers to Politicians.** Politicians don't take papers directly (that's "illegal"). Instead, you give papers to people called "lobbyists." The lobbyists give papers to "campaigns." The campaigns give papers to politicians. It's like money laundering but backwards and legal.

**Step 4: Give Papers to the Politicians' Friends.** Politicians have friends who run "Super PACs." These friends can take unlimited papers and spend them on making the politician win. This isn't bribery because you called it something else.

**Step 5: Give Papers Back to the Rich Humans (Forever).** The treaty passes, redirecting $27.2B in papers annually. Rich humans get 272% returns on what they gave you, forever. This is a good deal because forever is a long time. Unless you die from preventable diseases. Which you're fixing.

The financial instrument at the center of all this makes rich people richer every time the treaty expands and politicians richer every time they vote yes. The people who already control your government now have a financial reason to save your life. Nobody has to become a better person. (That's obviously out of the question.)

On Wishonia, we used this exact program 4,297 years ago. We liked it so much we pointed it at corruption, redundant agencies, regulations written before we discovered electricity, and everything else that was broken.

The universe is literally offering you infinite money and eternal life, and you're thinking about it. This is why aliens don't visit.

## Author Biography

Wishonia is an extradimensional observer who has been watching Earth since 1945, when humans split the atom and she assumed they were trying to unlock unlimited free energy. She has since been corrected.

Her research interests include why humans spend 604 times more on killing each other than on testing whether medicines work, why they named their planet Dirt, and whether they are capable of solving problems that don't involve pointing weapons at things. Preliminary findings are discouraging but not conclusive.

She has no formal credentials recognized by any human institution, which she considers a point in her favor given what those institutions have accomplished. Her methodology consists of observing what humans do, comparing it to what they should obviously do instead, and writing it down in a tone of polite disbelief.

This is her first book. She is not optimistic about a second one being necessary, but she is not optimistic in general.

## Translator Biography

Mike P. Sinn has spent 20 years building software to figure out what works and what doesn't in healthcare. He founded the Institute for Accelerated Medicine after realizing that the bottleneck to curing diseases isn't science; it's paperwork, misaligned incentives, and the fact that governments spend 604 times more on weapons than on testing whether medicines work.

He previously built the largest open-source platform for health data aggregation and analysis, collecting over 10 million data points on the effects of thousands of foods, drugs, and supplements on human health outcomes. He has published research on decentralized clinical trials, optimal resource allocation, and why the FDA approval process kills more people than it saves.

He translated Wishonia's observations into this book because he could not figure out how to say "stop spending money on murder and start spending it on medicine" in a way that didn't make people's eyes glaze over. Based on early feedback, the alien voice was only a partial improvement.

He lives on a planet called Dirt and can be reached at mike@warondisease.org.
